title: Sliding, swinging and rolling
target: Choose the energy terms that match the type of motion.
criteria: Distinguish translational and rotational kinetic energy.
Use equal height changes to compare ideal energy changes.
State when a simple point-mass model is insufficient.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A rigid wheel rolls along a surface. Which motion energies can it have?
options: Only potential energy because contact is stationary momentarily.
Only translational kinetic energy in every model.
cpa.guide: Its center translates while the wheel rotates.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A rolling object loses 32 J of gravitational potential energy. It gains 12 J of rotational energy with negligible losses. What is its translational energy gain?
cpa.guide: The 32 J splits into 12 J rotational and 20 J translational.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A sliding point mass and a swinging point mass start from rest and descend the same height without resistance. Compare final speeds.
options: Speed depends only on travel time.
Sliding must be faster because the path is straighter.
Swinging must be faster because the path is curved.
cpa.guide: For each point mass, ½mv² = mgΔh.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Two ideal point masses descend 0.8 m and 3.2 m from rest. What is the ratio of the second speed to the first?
cpa.guide: Speed scales with the square root of height; √(3.2/0.8) = 2.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A student assigns all lost gravitational energy to the center-of-mass motion of a rolling ball. What was omitted?
cpa.guide: Rolling can store energy in rotation as well as translation.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A rolling cylinder arrives slower than a frictionless sliding block after equal drops from rest. Does this alone prove energy loss?
options: Yes; any rotating body violates conservation.
No; the cylinder must gain mass instead.
No; some cylinder energy can be rotational.
Yes; speed alone measures every form of energy.
cpa.guide: Compare all energy terms before concluding that energy left the mechanical account.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
